body:
This is a consequence of Godot's dictionaries supporting more data types than JSON dictionaries, and also because `JSON.stringify()` is extremely lenient to errors (and in most cases doesn't even print errors/warnings; we only recently added a warning about serializing non-finite numbers, which aren't supported by JSON).

In my opinion, `JSON.stringify()` was intended for serializing fixed pre-known data structures or at least pre-validated values. Attempting to serialize an arbitrary value is a form of undefined behavior. If you want to support all Godot data types, you should use a different solution, such as `JSON.from_native()`:

```gdscript
var data := {"1": "a", 1: "b"}
print(JSON.stringify(JSON.from_native(data)))
# {"args":["s:1","s:a","i:1","s:b"],"type":"Dictionary"}
```

However, perhaps this case deserves some sort of fix, as it produces invalid (?) JSON. Perhaps the last key-value pair should overwrite earlier occurrences? Or vice versa? CC @aaronfranke

I'd like to hear from users on what the expected behavior should be. I wonder if we should require that Dictionary inputs use Strings? Or at a minimum suggest that in the documentation. And then if non-String things are used as keys, that may cause conflicts, so what should we do? Discard one or the other? Either option seems "bad". Maybe it should entirely fail the function? Note that this is invalid input to begin with, so arguably that would make sense.

> Maybe it should entirely fail the function?

Naturally.

As someone who writes code to deal with JSON frequently (and found the issue by writing a Reflection utility for GDScript), it should have been like that to begin with, but not for the reason you think.

The problem is you can only ever deserialize a JSON Object into a `Dictionary` with `String` keys in GDScript, were we able to specify the type being deserialized we could parse `{ "1": "a", "2": "b" }` into `Dictionary[int, String]` just fine, this is a mandatory reflection feature in strongly typed languages (which I acknowledge GDScript isn't).

In the possible world where you could deserialize into a specified type, the answer becomes obvious: Only allow serialization of typed dictionaries.

In my case, writing my Reflection utility (which naturally doesn't support deserializing untyped dictionaries at all), it is merely obvious to me that I should enforce that only typed dictionaries can be serialized, and if not that, at least type-consistent untyped dictionaries, such that the example for this issue fails.

**TL;DR: Either way, this will be a breaking change, so my suggestion would be to at the very least keep it as is and log an error while there is not a fix for it.**

---

To the usual, trite callbacks to using `JSON.from_native` and `JSON.to_native`: You miss the point entirely! Most of the time you're writing code for JSON it is to talk to an API, or your game's _very possibly not written in godot_ server, which not only doesn't parse Godot's custom schema natively, but also ought not to, for too may reasons anyone who isn't making online tic-tac-toe would tell you.

The goal of my Reflection utility is to be able to serialize `Vector2(1, 2)` into `{ "x": 1, "y": 2 }`, and back into `Vector2(1, 2)`, and same for every other struct-like classes and primitives native to gdscript to bypass that problem entirely. If you wanna hear about progress on this, `@ctraul` on Discord.
